workflow_register.purpose_scope: Select the appropriate cervical cancer screening method based on age and HPV test availability.

workflow_register.end_state: Appropriate screening method selected or client routed to the relevant screening workflow
workflow_register.notes: Derived from Fig 6 selection flowchart and screening-method narrative.

_provenance.table_figure_id: Fig 6: Flowchart for selection of screening method based on age
_provenance.evidence_excerpt: HPV testing is recommended as the primary screening method... Where HPV testing is not yet available, or loss-to-follow-up is a risk, then VIA is an acceptable primary screening method... Pap smear is recommended...

_derivation.explanation: Workflow synthesized directly from the age-based screening selection flowchart and supporting narrative.

workflow_register.purpose_scope: Perform HPV screening, triage HPV-positive clients, determine treatment eligibility, and route to treatment, follow-up, or referral.
workflow_register.end_state: Client treated, referred, or scheduled for follow-up based on results
workflow_register.notes: Includes screen-triage-and-treat and screen-and-treat branches from Fig 6 and Fig 7.

_provenance.table_figure_id: Fig 7: Algorithm for primary screening with HPV test
_provenance.evidence_excerpt: Women who are HPV-negative are not treated, nor evaluated further. Women who are HPV-positive should all be treated but first eligibility for ablative treatment must be assessed... Those who are ineligible... should be referred...

_derivation.explanation: Workflow derived from the HPV algorithm and accompanying narrative describing screen-and-treat and screen-triage-and-treat pathways.

workflow_register.purpose_scope: Perform VIA screening, interpret results, determine eligibility for ablation, and route positive or suspicious cases to treatment or referral.
workflow_register.end_state: Client treated, referred, or scheduled for rescreening/follow-up
workflow_register.notes: Derived from VIA narrative and Fig 9.

_provenance.table_figure_id: Fig 9: Algorithm for conducting visual inspection with acetic acid
_provenance.evidence_excerpt: VIA is appropriate to use in women whose squamocolumnar junction (SCJ) is visible... If the cervix shows any unusual signs or the provider suspects cancer, a punch biopsy should be collected or the patient can be referred...

_derivation.explanation: Workflow synthesized from VIA procedure steps, eligibility criteria, and VIA algorithm branches.

_provenance.evidence_excerpt: Collect the specimens from the face of the cervix and the endocervix... Cytotechnologists in the laboratory process and interpret it... If abnormal cells are seen... classified using the Bethesda System.
